shots.text: Red Bull paid thirteen million over its wings slogan.
Nobody expected real wings. So why did it pay?
Its marketing said the drink improves performance and concentration.
A customer named Benjamin Careathers sued. He argued the drink worked no better than the same caffeine in coffee.
His lawyers said this was not harmless puffery. It was deceptive advertising.
Red Bull said its marketing was always truthful and accurate.
But the case could reach everyone who had bought a can since two thousand two.
Millions of people. So Red Bull chose to settle, to avoid the cost and distraction of a long fight.
The deal was worth thirteen million dollars.
Buyers could claim ten dollars in cash, or fifteen dollars in Red Bull.
And Red Bull never admitted doing anything wrong.
Nobody grew wings. But Red Bull paid millions to make the case go away.
